title: Election Night: Polls Close and Counting Begins
summary:
On Tuesday, voters across the United States will finish choosing members of Congress and governors. Then the counting begins.

Polls close at different times in different states. The first close at 7 p.m. Eastern Time. The last, in Alaska, close at 1 a.m. Eastern Time. So results come in waves, state by state.

People will watch Georgia and Florida first. Georgia has races for the Senate and for governor. Its Secretary of State, Brad Raffensperger, told local news that counties must report results within an hour of polls closing. Florida has governor and Senate races, plus seven close House races, according to the Cook Political Report.

Later, close Senate races in North Carolina, Ohio, and other states could decide which party controls the Senate. That answer may take a long time. California counts slowly, and Alaska's results could take weeks. Counting could go on for days or even weeks.
why_it_matters: The leaders voters choose will help make decisions that affect families and children across the country.

keywords.explanation: Congress is the group of lawmakers in the United States who help make the country's laws.
A governor is the leader of a state government.
Polls are the places where people vote in an election, and they open and close at set times.
The Senate is one of the two parts of Congress, where each state has its own senators.
In an election, a race is a contest between people who each want to win the same job.

Close races can decide which party controls the Senate, and counting in some states can take days or even weeks.
